text:
maria_cs: FYI we just got a high-priority escalation from ACME—post-rollout codegen regression. Customer reports previously working TypeScript helper now causes tsc compile errors and missing imports/steps. They say this started immediately after yesterday's model rollout. Need ML + eng triage and rollback options. cc @tomasz_ml @ashley_eng :triage:

acme_engineer: Hey Redwood, after the update our build breaks during CI. It used to pass with generated helper code, now tsc fails with "Cannot find name 'HttpError'" and other missing types. We rely on the model to include imports and correct function signatures. Example prompt and model call we used below, plus the generated output. This used to work before your rollout. Please advise, this blocks our release.

Prompt (trimmed):
"""
Write a TypeScript helper to call our /users API and return typed User objects. Include imports and error handling. Use fetch.
"""

Generated output we received from the API (raw):
```ts
export async function getUser(userId: number): User {
  const response = fetch(`/api/users/${userId}`)
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new HttpError(response.status)
  }
  return await response.json()
}
```
TS compiler output when we try to build: 
```
src/gen/getUser.ts:1:38 - error TS2304: Cannot find name 'User'.
src/gen/getUser.ts:3:11 - error TS2304: Cannot find name 'HttpError'.
```
We used to get a generated file that included the interface and import for HttpError. Now both are missing.

lee_support: I attempted to repro locally calling the same endpoint with the same prompt against model rwd-3.2-ga (the rollout flagged yesterday). I can reproduce: same output and same tsc failures. Attached the exact API request we made using the Redwood SDK:
```js
const resp = await redwood.generate({
  model: 'rwd-3.2-ga',
  prompt: "Write a TypeScript helper to call our /users API and return typed User objects. Include imports and error handling. Use fetch.",
  temperature: 0.0,
  max_tokens: 320
})
console.log(resp.text)
```

dev-bot: deploy-bot: rollout "rwd-3.2-ga" (rollout-2026-04-21-09) completed at 1827649800.

ops-bot: metric-alert: observed a jump in generated_compile_errors for codegen templates around 1827649900. Baseline ~0.02% -> spike ~1.7% (5m window) :bar_chart:.

tomasz_ml: Thanks, looks actionable. Quick hypotheses: 1) a new code-style or post-processing filter stripped top-level imports/interfaces, 2) the finetune introduced a scaffold change (omitted interface/exports), or 3) tokenization changes under the new variant truncated the preface instructions. Can we get the raw candidates (no safety/post-process) and the model sampling seeds? @dev-bot can you attach raw-candidate outputs and rollout config?

ashley_eng: If ACME is blocked we should consider rolling back traffic for that org and model immediately. We can target org-scoped rollback while we investigate to reduce blast radius. Also need a minimal failing eval set to run across old vs new model.

jordan_se: Created INF-2319 (P1) for this escalation and linked customer case 54412. I've attached the sample prompt + generated output and tsc log. Assigned to @tomasz_ml and @ashley_eng.

maria_cs: Customer impact: 3 internal teams blocked, CI failing across their repos. They asked for rollback ASAP and a writeup of what changed. Please confirm ETA. :pray:

ashley_eng: I'll prepare a rollback for that org in ~5m unless someone objects. Plan: revert traffic for acme org (org-id:12233) to rwd-3.1-stable while ML investigates. Not planning a global rollback yet.

dev-bot: deploy-bot: initiating org-scoped rollback for org-id 12233 -> target model rwd-3.1-stable. trace_id=rollback-1827654300. ETA ~7m.

acme_engineer: Thank you. Can you also share what changed (diff) so we can update our prompt templates if needed? We rely heavily on the generator for consistent code scaffolding.

tomasz_ml: I'll run a diff between rwd-3.1-stable and rwd-3.2-ga on a small curated set including their prompt. Early local test shows rwd-3.2-ga tends to omit import statements and drop explicit interface definitions when the prompt is short. Two immediate mitigations: (A) recommend customers include explicit "Include imports and types: true" in the prompt, (B) enforce a post-generation compile-check in our pipeline and fallback to an alternate variant on failure. I'll post a short analysis and failing cases in this thread.

lee_support: I'll update the customer with rollback ETA and ask them to run CI once rollback completes. Also asked them to provide any other prompts they use so we can expand the eval set.

jordan_se: INF-2319 updated: action=rollback_in_progress, owners=[tomasz_ml,ashley_eng], link_to_customer_case=54412.

dev-bot: deploy-bot: rollback complete at 1827654360. Traffic for org-id 12233 switched to rwd-3.1-stable.

acme_engineer: Build passed after rollback, thanks for the quick help. We'll run full CI and confirm, and share any additional failing prompts. Could you follow up with a short explanation of what changed?

maria_cs: Customer confirmed build pass locally and in initial CI. I'll keep watch until they finish full run. Great job everyone. :tada:

tomasz_ml: Follow-up: we'll run a full regression suite comparing the two variants and share a postmortem with root cause and a mitigation plan (add compile checks to model onboarding, add prompt guidance, consider a small recovery patch that reintroduces import scaffolding). I'll post results in INF-2319 once available.

lee_support: I'll mark the case as "workaround in place: rollback" and keep it open until we have PR/patch and fixes live.

ops-bot: monitoring-note: post-rollback the generated_compile_errors metric returned to baseline within 3m.

ashley_eng: Action items: 1) ML to produce diff and root cause (tomasz_ml), 2) Eng to prepare org-scoped rollback/runbook for future incidents (ashley_eng), 3) CS to collect broader customer examples (maria_cs/lee_support).

jordan_se: I'll keep INF-2319 open and set target for initial RCA within 48 hours.

maria_cs: Thanks team — customer requested follow-up doc for their SREs explaining the change and the recommended prompt tweaks. I'll draft and share once tomasz posts the root-cause details. :white_check_mark:
